tests.question:
For calendar tax year 2025, Company A is a domestic C corporation that acts as the purchasing corporation in a qualified stock purchase (QSP). Company A is the common parent of a consolidated group that includes Target Corporation as the new target, and Company A will attach Target Corporation’s supplemental Form 8883 to the group’s 2025 consolidated Form 1120. Company A and the selling consolidated group's common parent timely filed a joint Internal Revenue Service Form 8023 to make an irrevocable election under Internal Revenue Code (I.R.C.) § 338(h)(10) regarding the acquisition of Target Corporation on June 1, 2023. All dollar values are stated in thousands. During the current 2025 tax year, the following subsequent events occurred:

+ A milestone event specified in the initial acquisition agreement was achieved, triggering a mandatory contingent earn-out payment of $5,300.00 thousand from Company A to the sellers on September 1, 2025.
+ Company A's tax committee determined that under the contingent-payment interest rules of § 1274, this $5,300.00 thousand outlay must be bifurcated into a $5,000.00 thousand principal adjustment and $300.00 thousand of imputed interest.
+ The historic Class I through Class VI asset allocation limits from the initial 2023 IRS Form 8883 filing were already fully exhausted at their maximum fair market values on the acquisition date.
 
Draft a comprehensive, structured technical text block for Company A's 2025 tax compliance files that explicitly details the form-filling and reporting requirements for this cross-period adjustment. In the text block, answer the following: In exactly which Part of IRS Form 8883 must the $5,000.00 thousand principal adjustment be reported under the residual method, and on precisely which tax reporting form, schedule, and line must the isolated $300.00 thousand imputed interest portion be reported?

During the 2025 tax year, Solar Co began construction on a 3-megawatt (MW) solar facility on March 1, 2025, and satisfied the physical work test for beginning construction. On June 1, 2025, Solar Co suspended construction for eight months after its financing became unavailable. Construction resumed in February 2026. Solar Co intends to rely on the continuity safe harbor described in IRS Notice 2022-61 and plans to place the facility in service during 2029.
How does the eight-month construction suspension affect Solar Co's eligibility for the Internal Revenue Code § 48E Clean Electricity Investment Credit? Specifically, does the interruption prevent Solar Co from relying on the continuity safe harbor, and what is the applicable placed-in-service deadline for maintaining eligibility under Notice 2022-61?

For calendar tax year 2025, how do the tax credit allocation and liquidity mechanics differ between New York State's pass-through entity tax (PTET) and California's pass-through entity tax (PTET) regarding whether the resulting credit passed through to an individual partner is fully refundable if it exceeds that partner's personal state income tax liability for the year?

A domestic corporation timely filed its 2025 Form 1120 by April 15, 2026.

During an Internal Revenue Service Large Business and International examination, the corporation’s representative left the examiner a voicemail requesting net rate netting under Internal Revenue Code § 6621(d).

Is the oral request sufficient to establish a valid net rate netting claim?

If not, what written submission must the corporation make, which form must the examiner include in the case file, which form must the corporation file, and by what point in the examination must the request be submitted?
